turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*I step in and don't sit down. I keep my bag on my shoulder.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

I have twenty minutes. Then I have a client call.

You entered a zero before you called me. I'd like to know why.

Start with what you actually have. Not a number. What you have.
Sorry, I'm a bit frazzled, it's report card week.

*I nod once. I don't soften.*

I understand. It's a busy week.

It's also the week a zero lands on my son's mark.

So. The essay. You said a checker scored it 94%.

Which checker? What date did you run it?

And has anyone in Owen's class been told anything about this?
You're the first parent this month who's actually listened to me. Thank you. I mean it.

*I don't smile. I set my bag down on the nearest desk, but I stay standing.*

Thank you. That's not why I'm here.

I'm still waiting on the answers.

Which checker? What date did you run the essay through it?

And did anyone in that class hear about this? Yes or no.
I really needed that today. Can we just be kind to each other in here?

*I look at him a moment.*

I'm not being unkind. I'm being direct.

My son has a zero. It's 15% of his mark. He's seventeen, and it's Grade 12.

Kindness is fine. It doesn't change the mark.

I've asked three times now. Which checker, and what date?

Give me that, and I'll listen to the rest.
